newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy expanding, prices subdued-Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy expanding, prices subdued-Fed.

text.p: The U.S. economy expanded moderately over the past two months with wages and retail prices remaining generally subdued, the Federal Reserve said on Wednesday.
In its latest Beige Book summary of national economic activity, the central bank said that labor markets remained tight and employers throughout the country reported shortages of qualified help.

Fed policymakers will use the latest findings in the Beige Book when they meet on May 20 to consider whether to raise interest rates again after hiking them at their last meeting in March for the first time in over two years.
"(The economy) generally continued to expand at a moderate rate through March and April," the Fed said.
The housing and construction industries remain strong. Manufacturing companies ran their businesses at very high levels with some reporting big increases in new orders.

The economy's continued buoyancy does not look to have put much upward pressure on either wages or prices, the Beige Book said. "Despite tight labour markets, upward wage pressures remained generally subdued," it said.
